what: Lamar Advertising owns outdoor advertising space: billboards along American highways, digital displays, advertising in airports and on transit systems. It has operated under the Lamar name since 1902.
customers: Local and national advertisers, from restaurants and lawyers to large consumer brands.
money: highway logo signs and transit advertising
moat: Billboard permits that local zoning laws make almost impossible to obtain today, which fixes the supply of roadside advertising space in each market.
risks: Advertising spending falls in a recession
Debt of about $5 billion against almost no cash
Local advertising has been weak in some categories
opportunities: Operating margin of 34% with a 67% gross margin
Converting static boards to digital raises revenue per site several times over
A dividend yield above 4% backed by stable local advertising
watch: Same-board revenue growth and the pace of digital conversions.
